title: [factory-setup-agent] Sandbox amended for the test runner — two follow-ups it surfaced
body:
The amendment episode for inadequacy report `002d0ba19faa9525` (from the gardening PR that adds the repo's first test runner) is done. `commands.test` in the sandbox manifest is no longer `null`, so the tests gate has something to run.

Two things came out of it that no other mechanism will record, so they are here.

## 1\. `commands.test` is `npm test --if-present`, not the literal `npm test`

The report asked for `npm test`. Taking that literally would have cost a round and frozen a *worse* sandbox than the one in place:

- `factory-setup-trial.yml` checks out the **default branch**. All five PRs that add a `test` script are still open, so the default branch has none, and bare `npm test` exits 1 there with `Missing script: "test"`.
- In the runner, `reachedTier` returns `static` as soon as the test step fails, and the run + screenshot sequence is skipped entirely because it is guarded on every prior step being ok.
- So the manifest would have measured `static` instead of `renders`, while still running nobody's tests.

`npm test --if-present` is the same command wherever a `test` script exists, and it was measured in all four places that decide whether it is honest:

| Where | Result |
| --- | --- |
| PR #15's tree, after `npm ci` | 4 tests, 0 failures, **exit 0** |
| ...with a deliberately failing test added | **exit 1** — a red test is not swallowed |
| Default branch today | exit 0, nothing run — the trial still reaches the app |
| Directory with no `package.json` | **exit 254** (so is bare `npm test`) — the trial's empty-directory control still shows the command depends on this repo |

`bsf gates tests` runs `commands.test` verbatim in the repo root against a PR's own head commit, where the script exists, so the gate gets the real run rather than the no-op.

**Follow-up:** once *any* runner is merged to the default branch, `npm test --if-present` and `npm test` are identical, and the plain form is strictly better — deleting the `test` script should fail the gate, not pass it quietly. That is a one-line amendment to `commands.test`. It is recorded in the manifest under `dropped` and `capabilities.not_exercised`, and in the runbook's Test section.

## 2\. Five open PRs are each adding the same first test runner

#11, #12, #13, #14 and #15 all independently add the repo's first runner. All five use node's built-in `node --test` with no new dependency, and all five are driven by `npm test` — which is why the manifest drives tests through npm rather than naming a runner. They disagree on the details:

- **Directory:** #14 and #15 use `test/`; #11, #12 and #13 use `tests/`.
- **Coverage:** #13 and #14 emit `coverage/lcov.info` via `--experimental-test-coverage`; #11, #12 and #15 do not.

Whichever merges first sets the convention, and also decides whether total coverage can be measured at all (nothing in the manifest records a coverage command). The other four will then conflict or duplicate.

This is a factory problem rather than a problem with any of those PRs: nothing told the second through fifth agent that the first had already added a runner. When a change is foundational — a runner, a formatter, a CI job — the queue should carry one item for it, not one per feature folder that notices it is missing. Recorded under Escalations in `history.md`.

## What else changed

Nothing. `install`, `build`, `run`, `seed`, `env`, `services`, `stubs` and `egress` are unchanged, and were all re-run to confirm the amendment costs nothing: `npm ci` exit 0; the server came up; `/health` → `ok`; the seed added three items and `/report` showed lines 3, units 16, value $297.37; `/export` returned the CSV with both headers; `/delete?id=2` → 302 with the total falling $297.37 → $237.49; and a full-page Chromium screenshot of `/` shows the heading, table, total, add form and export link. Still **renders**.

Guardrails were skipped, as they are on every amendment.
